forking_paths.verdict: E39 is a genuine confirmation on fresh streams for the quantity that is ranked; the forking paths across E36-E39 are in the control gate, not in the effect estimate, and they lower the evidential weight of C_F^post to near zero without creating the rank
forking_paths.fixed_across_the_series: The hypothesis (F, S, H cheaper than A and E25 at every weight), the rule code (unchanged since a86c6c846d), the pricing S(g) = total_muls + 97 g (macaulay_entries + selection) and the selection counting rule (§9.41, which extends E33's §9.35), the weights 0 / 0.1 / 1 GAE, the sensitivities sigma1-sigma3, the rank rule (every row, every weight), and the rows (E25's 20 GLS rows from E36, plus E24's 12 curves from E37). Rule K was dropped after E36 by its own registered prediction (it was the test of the selection bound and lost at 1 GAE as predicted); F, S, H were all registered in E36.
forking_paths.what_varied: Only the controls and the gate: E36's S/H inverse-map control corrupted rows the solve never reads (kill fired); E37 aimed its controls at rows the normal forms read, and C_F failed the strict positive check 0/320 (kill fired); E38 replaced the check by P_ext (repaired post hoc after diagnosing that a misfile always changes the pivot set and the border targets, then pre-registered and passed 160/160 on fresh pilots) and added C_F^mid, which could never be aimed (kill fired); E39 added C_F^post, designed so that its positive check holds by construction on any aimed call. The non-empty detection gate moved 0.95 -> 0.96 using pooled E37 + E38 rates.
forking_paths.effect_replicated: The ranked quantity is a deterministic paired count, and it has been measured on three independent target streams with frozen code: S_A/S_F at 0 / 0.1 / 1 GAE was 1.464-1.528 / 1.094-1.105 / 1.0115-1.0128 in E36 (20 rows, existing stream), 1.466-1.539 / 1.0944-1.1065 / 1.0116-1.0130 in E37 (32 rows, 0xE37E0001) and 1.457-1.537 / 1.094-1.106 / 1.0115-1.0130 in E39 (32 rows, 0xE39E0001); per row the E39 - E37 difference is at most 0.0111 / 0.0010 / 8.3e-5. Within E39's Stage A, F is cheaper than A on 10,000/10,000 paired calls at every weight. No choice made after seeing data can have moved these numbers: they are produced by frozen code on fresh streams and every arm sees the same calls.
forking_paths.residual_risk: Re-designing a gate until it passes is a forking path for the decision to rank, not for the size of the effect. The risk it carries is that a real defect of F (wrong outputs, undercounted work) survives because the passing gate is insensitive to it. That risk is addressed directly rather than by the controls: output identity is checked on every call and every record, the counter is checked exactly by the positive control, and C_F (a defect specific to F's filing) is detected. C_F^post, the control introduced for E39, passes by construction and should not be read as independent evidence about F.
forking_paths.scope: Fresh streams change the targets and residuals, not the curves: E39 replicates over targets on the same 32 curve instances (same factor bases and precomputes). It is not a replication over new curves or sizes.

controls_finding.verdict: sufficient for the rank claim as stated, with C_F^post carrying almost no independent weight
controls_finding.what_the_rank_needs: The claim is that F, S and H reach the same outputs as A with fewer counted F_p multiplications and no more native operations. It needs (a) output identity on every call, (b) a counter that counts F's echelon by the same rule as A's, (c) all selection work of each rule priced, and (d) evidence that the identity comparison would see a defect in the rules' echelon.
controls_finding.how_each_is_met: (a) Direct comparison with the existing solver on each of the 10,000 Stage A calls (in-binary, replayed byte for byte) and the validator's independent leaf-by-leaf comparison of all 160 end-to-end row records with A's (logs, relations, decompositions, lifted points, rational solutions, fallbacks, entries and walks equal). (b) The positive control A's rule through E36's echelon reproduces A counted's call total, echelon count, lead scans and digest on 10,000/10,000 calls, so the new echelon's counter equals E33's under the same pivot sequence, and F differs only in which row it takes. (c) F and L selection is 0 on every call (and the harness checks it); S's and H's counted work matches §9.41's rule (S about 512 per call: one per coefficient examined, one per row moved, comparisons; H = S + one branch per contested column, 334). (d) Detection on non-empty calls is 0.990-1.000 for every gating control. F's and L's digests differ from A's on every contested call, so the rules really pivot differently, and the perturbed coefficient changes every non-empty set.
controls_finding.C_F_post: C_F^post is mechanically almost the calibration C_0, as the producer says. Both move one entry of a row the normal forms read after its last echelon use, and they are detected at the same rate: C_F^post 271/320 (193/194 non-empty), C_0 on F 268/320 (192/194). Its positive check P_post holds by construction on every aimed call (pivot set and border targets cannot change), so 320/320 positive is an implementation check, not an empirical result. What it does add: the altered row is one F chose at a contested column (|bucket| > 1) that the normal forms read, with the structure provably intact, so a content error in F's choices reaches the identity comparison on 99.5 % of non-empty calls. It does not test whether F's choice is right; no control does, and the claim does not need one. Any pivot choice spans the same row space, and correctness is checked on outputs.
controls_finding.C_F_P_ext: C_F under P_ext (E37's misfile: the second arrival at c* skips its update and is filed by its next nonzero) is the only control that exercises a defect in F's own filing logic. It always changes the pivot set and the border targets (320/320), so the strict check never holds and P_ext does. It is detected on 316/320 calls (192/194 non-empty), 315 of them through the fallback flag alone: the defect makes the chain solve fail its own consistency check and rerun the existing solver, which then returns correct outputs. That is a real detection under the registered rule, because Stage A requires the same fallback calls for every chain solver (identical on 10/10 curves) and the end to end requires the same fallback count per row (32/32). It also means an F filing defect would cost extra fallbacks, which the band prices.
controls_finding.weaknesses: (1) Every control runs on E25's ten GLS curves only; on E24's 12 curves the rules are covered only by the end-to-end identity. (2) On calls with an empty clean set, detection is weaker (C_F^post 78/126, C_SH (S) 82/126, C_F 124/126 through fallbacks), so empty-set calls are weaker witnesses; but output identity is checked on them directly. (3) Most detections (182-315 per control) come through the fallback flag alone, so the detector depends on the chain solve's self-check. (4) The P_ext repair and C_F^post were designed after earlier failures (see forking_paths).
controls_finding.null_object: This is a deterministic paired count, not a statistical correlation, so inventor-protocol §3's null object does not apply literally. The rule-level negative control is L (zero selection work, worst arrival order). It is measured behind A on 32/32 rows at every weight and on 10,000/10,000 paired calls, so the instrument does not favour an arbitrary zero-cost rule. A random-order rule (the literal null object) was not run; that is a limitation, not a failure.
